key_insight: PP-VarQITE designs shallow thermal-state preparation circuits entirely classically, encoding temperature in the angles of a fixed circuit architecture.
engineering_relevance: Reducing circuit depth makes low-temperature quantum simulation more practical on noisy hardware without requiring quantum measurements during parameter optimization.
method: Combine Pauli propagation with variational quantum imaginary-time evolution.
Determine temperature-dependent circuit parameters entirely classically.
Execute the resulting shallow circuits on trapped-ion hardware.
evidence_signal: Numerical tests reached 100 qubits and yielded circuits approximately 2–10× shallower than sequential tensor-network compilation baselines; Quantinuum Helios experiments used 96 and 98 qubits, with the Ising lattice requiring at most 42 two-qubit layers.
watch_item: The reported depth advantage is model- and baseline-specific; classical optimization costs and robustness on other hardware require further evaluation.
paper_title: Thermal state preparation with shallow quantum circuits
